article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 70% Indica / 30% Sativa
Genetics: Now N Later × Jet Fuel Gelato
Breeder: Compound Genetics
THC Content: 23–30%
CBD Content: Low, generally below 1%
Terpene Profile: Myrcene , caryophyllene , pinene
Primary Flavors: Apple, banana, cherry, tropical fruit
Flowering Time (Indoor): 60–70 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September through October
Indoor Yield: Medium to high
Outdoor Yield: High potential
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Apples & Bananas helped define the modern era of fruit-forward cannabis without sacrificing the gas, potency, and resin production sought by experienced marijuana consumers. Developed by Compound Genetics and brought to prominence through its collaboration with Cookies, the cultivar produces dark, trichome-heavy flowers carrying an unusually broad aroma: fresh tree fruit, ripe banana, cherry, pastry-like sweetness, spice, and fuel can all appear from the same cured bud.

Behind that dessert-like presentation is formidable potency. Verified commercial examples routinely land in the upper-20% THC range, while the experience combines a strong cerebral rush with a lighter, floating sensation through the body. Cookies currently identifies the original Compound Genetics cross as Now N Later × Jet Fuel Gelato and describes the flavor as baked apple pie and banana pudding over a gassy finish.
Genetics and Lineage

The most defensible current pedigree is Now N Later × Jet Fuel Gelato. That is the lineage published by Cookies for its Apples & Bananas flower and explicitly attributed to original breeder Compound Genetics. The genetics are sometimes presented as [( Platinum Cookies × Granddaddy Purple ) × Blue Power] × Gelatti , which appears contradictory until the deeper ancestry is considered. Historical descriptions connect Now N Later with Platinum Cookies, Granddaddy Purple, and Blue Power ancestry, which is why those names repeatedly appear in expanded versions of the family tree. Cookies itself has published both the current Now N Later × Jet Fuel Gelato specification and discussion of that more complex breeding background.

Now N Later contributes much of the dark fruit, sweetness, color potential, and dense modern flower structure. Its broader family incorporates Cookies, Granddaddy Purple, and Blue Power influences, creating a foundation rich in berry, grape, dessert, and resin traits. Jet Fuel Gelato supplies a more aggressive side of the personality, adding vigorous growth, floral-gas aromatics, potency, and the sharp fuel quality that keeps Apples & Bananas from tasting like straightforward fruit candy.

The cross became one of Compound Genetics’ defining cultivars and later served as breeding material for numerous projects. Compound’s current catalog continues using Apples & Bananas in hybrids such as A.B. Parfait and Goofiez², and the company describes the parent as contributing tropical fruit, apple-like sweetness, strong trichome coverage, swollen calyxes, and vigorous growth. That continuing use is a strong indication of the strain’s importance within Compound’s breeding program.
Effects and Experience

Apples & Bananas can feel considerably more forceful than its playful name suggests. The opening commonly concentrates in the head, producing an immediate euphoric shift that can make conversation, music, food, and entertainment seem unusually engaging. Mood tends to rise quickly, sometimes accompanied by a burst of creativity or free-flowing thought. Cookies describes the experience as a heavy head high combined with a floating body sensation, which captures the strain’s unusual balance well.

Physical effects become easier to notice after the initial cerebral surge. Rather than dropping suddenly into couch-lock, relaxation spreads gradually and creates a loose, buoyant feeling through the limbs. At moderate amounts, the consumer may remain social and mentally active even as the body becomes more comfortable. Larger servings bring the indica side forward, turning the same cannabis into a heavier evening experience.

Potency is substantial. Commercial genetic libraries document THC around 23–30%, while Cookies Thailand lists a tested example at 28.1% THC and only 0.06% CBD. Such numbers place Apples & Bananas firmly in experienced-consumer territory. People with limited THC tolerance may find even a modest amount surprisingly intense, especially during the fast cerebral onset.
Medical Benefits

The combination of mood elevation and physical relaxation explains why some medical marijuana consumers gravitate toward Apples & Bananas. Its early mental lift may appeal to people seeking temporary relief from stress, low mood, or reduced motivation, while the later body component can make the cultivar attractive when physical tension accompanies those concerns. The experience generally remains more mentally engaging than the heavy sedation associated with traditional Afghan-style weed.

Still, Apples & Bananas has not been clinically demonstrated to treat depression, anxiety, chronic pain, insomnia, or another specific disorder. Individual cannabis strains can also vary substantially between farms and batches. A flower testing near 30% THC may produce a dramatically different medical experience than material carrying lower potency or a different terpene balance.

Its low CBD content is another important consideration. This is primarily THC-dominant marijuana rather than a balanced medicinal strain, and large servings can potentially increase anxiety, dizziness, or cognitive impairment in sensitive consumers. Medical users should place more weight on the laboratory analysis of the actual product than on generalized strain reputation.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Fruit dominates the first impression, but Apples & Bananas is considerably more complex than its name. Cookies describes aromas of cherry, apple, banana, and gas, while the flavor has been compared with baked apple pie followed by creamy banana pudding. Breaking apart a mature flower can also reveal berry, tropical fruit, pepper, floral perfume, and an earthy mineral quality beneath the sweeter surface.

The inhale often begins with crisp apple-like fruit and creamy sweetness. Banana develops more clearly through the middle, followed by spice, cherry, and darker berry notes. Fuel becomes increasingly noticeable on the finish, giving the smoke enough sharpness to counteract the dessert character. Depending on phenotype, some flowers lean toward creamy pastry while others become markedly gassier.

Laboratory profiles vary, but several documented examples point toward myrcene as an important terpene. Segra reports elevated myrcene, ocimene, and pinene in its Apples N Bananas selection, while other genetic libraries identify combinations including limonene and caryophyllene. This variation fits the strain’s complicated aroma: tropical sweetness, fresh fruit, floral notes, pepper, and gas can all emerge from slightly different terpene ratios.
Growing Information

Apples & Bananas grows with more vigor than its dense finished flowers might suggest. Genetic nursery records describe high vegetative speed, medium-to-tall height, substantial stretch, and medium-to-high or heavy yield potential. A verified Compound Genetics selection maintained by Segra lists a 63-day flowering period, high stretch, heavy production, and elongated conical flowers, while Node Labs gives approximately nine weeks of flowering and medium-to-high yields.

Indoor growers should manage vertical growth before the stretch becomes difficult to control. Topping during vegetative growth encourages stronger secondary branches and produces a flatter canopy, while a trellis can help distribute the plant’s weight as the large calyxes swell late in bloom. Phinest’s cultivation notes recommend roughly three to four weeks of vegetative growth after topping and describe the cultivar as having excellent structure, strong purple expression, and occasional foxtailing. A nine-week target is appropriate for many plants, although some phenotypes may need closer to 65–70 days.

Outdoor cultivation can produce much larger plants when roots have unrestricted space and sunlight remains strong. Because the original breeder does not publish a reliable gram-per-plant outdoor specification, exact production claims should be treated cautiously. Warm days, adequate feeding, structural support, and relatively dry conditions during the final weeks give the cultivar its best opportunity to develop dense, resinous flowers without mold pressure. Cooler late-flowering nights may also intensify its purple coloration.
FAQ
Is Apples & Bananas an indica or sativa?

Apples & Bananas is generally treated as an indica-dominant hybrid, although classification varies somewhat by source and phenotype. Verified Compound genetic-library material describes the cultivar as approximately 70% indica and 30% sativa. Its effect still includes a pronounced cerebral and euphoric component.
What are the genetics of Apples & Bananas?

Cookies currently identifies the original Compound Genetics cross as Now N Later × Jet Fuel Gelato. Expanded ancestry frequently lists Platinum Cookies, Granddaddy Purple, and Blue Power because those genetics are associated with the Now N Later side of the family.
How much THC does Apples & Bananas have?
Potency is typically high. Documented genetic-library examples range around 23–30%, while Cookies has published individual flower around 28% THC. Actual batches can test outside that range.
What does Apples & Bananas taste like?
Expect apples, ripe banana, cherry, tropical fruit, creamy sweetness, spice, and a noticeable gasoline finish. Cookies specifically compares the flavor with baked apple pie and banana pudding.
How long does Apples & Bananas take to flower?

Approximately nine weeks is a reliable reference. Compound-linked nursery selections list around 63 days, while other documented cuts fall between roughly 60 and 70 days depending on phenotype and growing conditions.
Final Thoughts on Apples & Bananas

Apples & Bananas helped establish Compound Genetics as one of the defining breeders of modern American cannabis because it succeeds on several fronts simultaneously. The plant produces striking dark flowers, swollen calyxes, abundant resin, high THC, vigorous growth, and a fruit profile that genuinely resembles its name. Now N Later provides the layered fruit and dessert foundation while Jet Fuel Gelato adds the floral fuel and potency necessary to keep the cultivar from becoming one-dimensional.

Its reputation is therefore about considerably more than novelty flavor. Growers get a vigorous, medium-to-high yielding weed plant that generally finishes in about nine weeks, while consumers encounter a strong progression from heady euphoria into a relaxed, floating body sensation. Apples, banana pudding, cherry, tropical fruit, spice, and gas give the flower an instantly recognizable aromatic signature. In a market crowded with fruit-named hybrids, Apples & Bananas remains important because its combination of flavor, potency, appearance, and breeding influence helped shape the direction of contemporary premium cannabis.
